newsitem.title: USA: Rite Aid to buy two drug store chains in Deep South.
newsitem.headline: Rite Aid to buy two drug store chains in Deep South.

text.p: Rite Aid Corp., expanding into the South, said Monday it agreed to buy two privately held drug store chains with more than 330 stores in Louisiana, Alabama, Mississippi, Texas, Tennessee and Florida.

Rite Aid, already one of the nation's largest drugstore chains, with more than 3,600 stores in 27 states, did not disclose the terms of its acquisitions of K&B Services Inc. of New Orleans and Harco Inc. of Tuscaloosa, Ala.
The deals will give Rite Aid a total store count of 3,963 in 31 states.
K&B, the nation's 13th-largest drugstore chain, had fiscal 1996 sales of $580 million from 186 stores in Louisiana, Alabama, Mississippi, Texas, Tennessee and Florida.
Harco, the 17th largest chain, has 146 stores in Alabama, Mississippi and Florida. It had fiscal 1996 sales of $258 million, according to Rite Aid.
Rite Aid said it expected the deals to add to earnings by the second quarter of next year.

"The addition of two preeminent Southern drugstore chains gives Rite Aid a strong regional nucleus of operations and establishes a solid platform from which to expand our business in this fast-growing area of the country," Chairman Martin L. Grass said in a statement.
Following completion of these acquisitions, all K&B and Harco stores will be operated under the Rite Aid banner and all their store employees will be retained.
However, Rite Aid said it will close the Harco and K&B corporate offices and transfer all headquarters functions to Rite Aid headquarters in Camp Hill, Pa.
Rite Aid's stock lost 25 cents to $47.75 in early trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
